Ugh, fine. I know that to convert to base 10, I multiply the digits by the power of the base. So for $\Diamond4_7$, it would be $\Diamond \times 7^1 + 4 \times 7^0$, which is just $7\Diamond + 4$. Is that the right start?

Your approach to converting the base-7 number into a base-10 expression is correct. You've correctly identified the place values. Now, try applying that same logic to the other side of the equation, $\Diamond1_{8}$.

Okay, so $\Diamond1_{8}$ becomes $8\Diamond + 1$. That means the equation is $7\Diamond + 4 = 8\Diamond + 1$. Subtracting $7\Diamond$ from both sides gives $4 = \Diamond + 1$, and subtracting 1 gives $\Diamond = 3$. I'm 99% sure it's 3. Can you just tell me I'm right this one time?
